paragraph: Angola's [2025 state budget report](<https://www.opais.ao/politica/tribunais-arrancam-com-digitalizacao-de-processos-para-conferir-maior-celeridade/>) said the common-jurisdiction courts would start an integrated information and document system that year. It gave the judicial council over Kz 1 billion for it. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no later source says the system went live in any court. No source since November 2023 says cases can be filed online. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[Wearetech reported in October 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/burundi-la-numerisation-de-la-justice-face-au-defi-de-la-connectivite>) that Burundi is preparing an E-Justice platform to link the penal chain from judicial police to prisons. It is also to manage and keep judicial case files. In the last twelve months, [the platform was presented at a justice-sector meeting on 2 October 2026](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundis-e-justice-platform-to-allow-online-criminal-complaints-and-case-tracking/>), with UNDP support. No source says it is in use. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[La Marina BJ reported in August 2024](<https://lamarina.bj/2024/08/29/ou-en-est-on-avec-linterconnexion-des-juridictions-au-benin/>) that Benin's e-justice information system for criminal and civil procedures was at technical feasibility study. A consultancy was to be named by September 2024. In the last twelve months, since 16 February 2026, [three filings at the Cotonou Commercial Court are made online only](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/02/13/benin-trois-nouveaux-e-services-desormais-operationnels-au-tribunal-de-commerce-de-cotonou/>). No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The digital transition ministry said in June 2025](<https://www.mdenp.gov.bf/details?cHash=c0bdd7c3c4556fca9f1b0e43d15a0137&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Bnews%5D=974>) that a 2025-2027 project to digitise Burkina Faso's criminal and administrative judicial chains is under way. A development team is at work and the first works are in progress. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[In May 2025 the Chief Registrar told Parliament the Court Record Management System was obsolete everywhere but Gaborone](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/86398>). The judiciary was hiring a firm to expand it. In the last twelve months, [the justice ministry said in March 2026 that its Case Management System had not worked, because of system errors](<https://www.thegazette.news/news/paper-shortage-crisis-hits-courts/>). [The same month the minister said the Industrial Court had built its own electronic system](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202603170027.html>). No source found since November 2023 shows a court case management system working in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The Justice Minister announced on 29 June 2026](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2642911/societe/e-justice-les-39-tribunaux-de-premiere-instance-desormais-connectes-au-reseau-numerique-ivoirien>) that all 39 common-law first-instance courts in Côte d'Ivoire are connected to the e-Justice platform. It serves nationality certificates and criminal-record extracts. In the last twelve months it spread from two pilot courts in January 2025 and 28 courts by April 2026 to all 39. [In June 2025 he said all judicial procedures would be digitised in the short term](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2634927/politique/tribunal-de-1re-instance-dabidjan-le-ministre-sansan-kambile-lance-la-plateforme-digitale-e-justiceci>). No source says courts manage their cases on it. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

No stage is set. The only row found is the Supreme Court's case-processing software, which dates from January 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since November 2023 says how courts manage their cases. Preparing would need a source showing a case management or e-justice system procured, piloted in some courts or being built.

[UNDP says SIGAJ](<https://www.undp.org/fr/drcongo/actualites/transition-de-la-justice-congolaise-lalliance-onu-suede-au-service-de-letat-de-droit>), a system for managing judicial cases, was one of four systems introduced in the DR Congo justice sector between 2020 and 2024. In the last twelve months, [on 5 November 2026 the Ministry of Justice began linking courts, prosecutors and prisons](<https://actualite.cd/2026/11/05/rdc-lue-et-le-pnud-accompagnent-la-digitalisation-de-la-justice-pour-renforcer-la>). [In June 2026 FOLUCCO said it would soon pilot digitising the Gombe peace court](<https://folucco.cd/justice-2-0-un-projet-pilote-de-digitalisation-des-juridictions-bientot-lance-a-kinshasa/>). No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to file cases or documents online.

[Law 38/X/2024 says](<https://imij-cms.gov.cv/uploads/SIJ_Aprovado_Lei_38_IX_2024_28_de_marco_eff33d2257.pdf>) that Cabo Verde's Justice Information System has been phased in over a decade to support electronic handling of cases in the courts. The same law says its mass use in the courts has been held back. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to be able to file cases or documents with the courts online.

[UNDP reported for 2024](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-07/undp_djibouti_annual_report_en_v2.pdf>) that Djibouti's pilot digital case management system for minor offences was under construction, designed with judges and court administrators. It followed a review of digital readiness and a mapping of court processes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[On 22 September 2026 the Minister of Justice extended the national electronic window](<https://www.lejourdalgerie.com/extension-des-services-du-guichet-electronique-national-aux-cours-administratives-dappel-et-au-conseil-detat/>) to the administrative courts of appeal and the Council of State. Algerian litigants and their lawyers can follow cases on it and read the operative part of judgments. In the last twelve months, [electronic exchange of civil requests and reply briefs became compulsory for lawyers at the courts of justice from 18 January 2026](<https://fildalgerie.dz/justice-numerique-lechange-electronique-des-documents-et-le-paiement-en-ligne-obligatoires-des-janvier-2026/>). Fildalgerie reported the rule in December 2025.

[Egypt's Ministry of Justice launched the E-Court platform on 31 August 2026](<https://manassa.news/en/news/33836>) for the first-instance criminal courts. Lawyers get certified digital copies of case files and pay fees online. In the last twelve months, [the Council of State widened its e-litigation pilot in November 2026](<https://www.youm7.com/story/2026/11/8/%D8%B1%D8%A6%D9%8A%D8%B3-%D9%85%D8%AC%D9%84%D8%B3-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%B3%D8%B9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B6%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%8A-%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%81-%D8%AA%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%B9%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A9/7610749>) to the Education Administrative Court and the Health Disciplinary Court, where a disciplinary suit can be filed fully electronically. No source found since November 2023 says judgments are published online. Mature would need court decisions published online or the public able to look up a case's status online.

No stage is set. The only row found for Eritrea is a High Court case management system, dated 2001. That row is too old to set a stage. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since November 2023 says how courts manage their cases. Preparing would need a source from the past three years showing a case management or e-justice system procured, piloted in some courts or being built.

[Addis Fortune reported in July 2025](<https://addisfortune.news/supreme-court-sets-bold-course-toward-digital-justice>) that Ethiopia's Federal Supreme Court planned eCourt pilots from September 2025, with full rollout by August 2026. INSA is building the court management information system and a records system for about 2.2 billion Br. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says the pilots began or that the system went live in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[3News reported in February 2025](<https://3news.com/news/e-justice-ghanas-judiciary-leverages-dpi-to-enhance-justice-delivery>) that Ghana's e-justice system registers cases and allocates them to courts and judges, and that lawyers file cases and legal processes on it online. The Judicial Service put the cases filed on it at about 75,829 by January 2025. In the last twelve months, [the Labari Journal reported in December 2025 that it was still being rolled out](<https://labarijournal.com/is-ghanas-3-million-ejustice-system-is-underdelivering/>). An IMF governance report of 2024 said it had stalled. No source found since November 2023 says judgments or case status are open to the public online. Mature would need court decisions published online or the public able to look up a case's status online.

A [12-month consultancy signed on 7 September 2026](<http://www.ucepguinee.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AVIS-PUBLICATION-DE-LATTRIBUTION-INFORMATISATION-TCC.pdf>) is to set up an integrated management, archive and communication system at Guinea's Conakry commercial court. In the last twelve months, Guinea's procurement unit published the award on 5 October 2026. A private firm, Judicalex, [says it has digitised the court's decisions](<https://judicalex-gn.org/blog/post/tribunal-du-commerce-le-ministre-de-la-justice-ibrahima-sory-2-tounkara-decouvre-les-installations-de-judicalex/>) and put its hearing roll online. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The Office of the Chief Justice said in August 2024](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/judiciary-receives-vital-support-from-usaid>) that The Gambia's electronic case management system was in pilot. In the last twelve months, [in January 2026 the Chief Justice said lost donor funding had slowed it](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/judiciary-still-faces-shortage-of-courtrooms-and-office-space>), and he still awaited its implementation. In March 2026 UNDP [sought bids to build an integrated system](<https://www.ungm.org/Public/Notice/296129>) for the Judiciary and two ministries. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

In October 2024 [the Supreme Court signed an agreement with UNDP](<https://ahoraeg.com/politica/2024/10/07/la-corte-suprema-de-justicia-de-guinea-ecuatorial-y-pnud-firman-un-acuerdo-en-materia-de-digitalizacion/>) for digital systems in three Equatorial Guinea courts: the Supreme Court and the Malabo and Bata provincial courts. The court paid 90 million FCFA toward equipment to digitise case files. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says the systems are in service, or that cases can be filed online. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

Kenya's courts run their registries on the Case Tracking System, which [the Judiciary's 2023-24 report says](<https://www.judiciary.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/POPULAR-VERSION-SOJAR-REPORT-FY-2023_24.pdf>) covers case registration, fee assessment, cause lists and court orders. User accounts rose from 7,152 to 51,729. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [On 11 March 2024 e-filing reached all courts](<https://judiciary.go.ke/judiciary-launches-e-filing-in-all-courts-data-tracking-dashboard-and-causelist-portal-portal/>), extended from 17 counties to the other 34, with a Causelist Portal that lets anyone find when and where a case is to be heard.

[The Finance Minister said in July 2026](<https://informernewspaperliberia.com/ngafuan-hails-sovereign-ownership-of-pmtp-as-govt-funds-90-of-magistrate-training/>) that the Judiciary's 2026-2030 Strategic Plan puts an electronic case management system in all of Liberia's circuit courts, with e-filing and virtual hearings. In the last twelve months, the Judiciary's budget rose by 80% to US$33.3 million in 2026, with part of it for digitising legal records. [A May 2025 vacancy notice said the Judiciary was deploying an electronic case system for all courts](<http://judiciary.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ICT-Vacancy-Announcement.pdf>). No source says it is in service. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[In November 2026 Khalifa Ashour of the Attorney General's Office said](<https://www.vetogate.com/5764136>) that more than 1.2 million cases had been entered in the office's digital system. They date back to 1994 and carry all their documents. In the last twelve months, he said, the office also entered each hearing, judgment and appeal since 2025. No source found since November 2023 says cases can be filed with Libya's courts online. None says judgments or case status are published online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to file cases or documents online.

[The High Court rules of 2024 define e-justice](<https://lesotholii.org/akn/ls/act/ln/2024/65/eng@2024-06-21/source>) in Lesotho for serving process and keeping case files. Its start date awaits a gazette notice. In the last twelve months, [the Chief Justice said on 3 July 2026](<https://www.lena.gov.ls/national-dialogue-marks-a-new-chapter-for-lesotho-sakoane/>) that the Judiciary is putting digital systems in place, including electronic filing of court documents, with the Ministry of Information. No source since November 2023 says anyone files online yet, or that a court case management system is in service. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[Lawyers file requests, briefs and appeals through a dedicated platform](<https://telquel.ma/instant-t/2025/01/30/justice-voici-les-grandes-lignes-du-projet-du-dossier-judiciaire-electronique_1915535/>) in Morocco, the minister said in January 2025. [The ministry's portal says](<https://mahakim.ma/>) pleadings go straight to the chosen court, and fees are paid online. [The Mahakim tracking service](<https://mahakim.ma/>) lets the public follow civil and criminal files and hearing dates by file number. In the last twelve months, [the justice minister told MPs on 2 November 2026](<https://justice.gov.ma/2026/11/03/16889/>) that the electronic case file is being generalised. The cost is about MAD 2.5 billion, with digital notification.

[The Justice Ministry's secretary general said in June 2026](<https://www.lexpress.mg/2026/06/justice-numerique-la-gestion-des.html>) that InfoTA, InfoTF, LogiComm, LogiCivil and LogiPénal are deployed in Madagascar's courts. In the last twelve months, that statement listed tools for administrative, land, commercial, civil and criminal cases. In 2019 [such software ran in six first-instance courts](<https://prea.gov.mg/realisations/informatisation-des-juridictions-tatpitf/>) and in administrative and financial courts. No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to be able to file cases or documents with the courts online.

[The Ministry of Justice said in July 2026](<http://news.abamako.com/h/305410.html>) that Mali's e-Justice platform first serves nationality certificates and criminal records, with a second phase to manage judicial files. In the last twelve months, [on 5 November 2026 UNDP handed over equipment worth USD 493,193](<https://www.maliweb.net/economie/developpement/modernisation-de-la-justice-renforcement-de-letat-de-droit-le-pnud-3121305.html>) to run it. [In February 2026 the minister said an integrated case system was in pilot, with eight courts already linked](<https://lesoirdebamako.com/2026/02/11/semaine-nationale-de-la-justice-la-delivrance-digitale-du-casier-judiciaire-et-du-certificat-de-nationalite-lancee-hier/>). No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

No stage is set. [The Supreme Court launched a Portal de Jurisprudência and a Portal de Legislação](<https://oam.org.mz/oam-destaca-importancia-dos-portais-de-legislacao-e-jurisprudencia-para-a-transparencia-e-confianca-na-justica/>), the Bar Association reported in October 2026, and the first gives online access to the courts' decisions. In the last twelve months, that October 2026 launch is the only dated step found. No source found since November 2023 says courts are building or using a case management system. Preparing would need a source showing a case management or e-justice system procured, piloted in some courts or being built.

[On 4 February 2025 Mauritania's justice minister chaired a meeting on the sector's digitisation projects](<https://www.ami.mr/archives/219925>). The digital transformation minister and the head of the population register agency attended. Their three bodies are digitising the criminal justice chain, to let lawyers and parties follow their files, and commercial cases from registration to judgment, appeal and cassation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

A government list of operational systems from November 2024 [names a case management system for the Children's Court](<https://cib.govmu.org/Documents/Reports/List%20of%20Operational%20Systems.pdf>) in Mauritius, and a Supreme Court registry system. Since January 2021 attorneys at the Commercial Division [must file written submissions online](<https://ejudiciary.govmu.org/>), a rule that stood on the judiciary's notices page as of October 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says judgments or case status are open to the public online. Mature would need court decisions published online or the public able to look up a case's status online.

[The Judiciary's April 2024 concept note says](<https://judiciary.mw/sites/default/files/2024-04/E-COURT%20LAUNCH.pdf>) that digital case management platforms have already been introduced in Malawi's courts. Its e-court linked ten courts, six prisons and four police stations in a pilot. [In August 2025 a tender for the Zomba High Court registry said its records were all kept by hand](<https://ppda.mw/storage/documents/opentenders/Expression%20of%20Interest%20EoI%20Court%20Case%20Management%20System%202025-26.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to be able to file cases or documents with the courts online.

[The Chief Justice said in July 2025](<https://www.namibian.com.na/namibia-to-implement-e-justice-system-in-supreme-court/>) that Namibia's Supreme Court remains entirely on paper, and that a task force is defining an integrated case management system. In May 2025 [a Namibian delegation studied Uganda's system](<https://judiciary.go.ug/data/news/1683/Namibian%20Judiciary%20Team%20Concludes%20ECCMIS%20Benchmarking%20Visit%20to%20Uganda.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. In 2018 [eJustice served the High Court civil stream](<https://nacmnet.org/wp-content/uploads/NAMIBIA_NACM-Nomination-Form-Namibia-eJustice.pdf>). No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

Nigeria's Supreme Court launched the Nigerian Case Management System on 1 July 2026. [The Chief Justice said](<https://tribuneonlineng.com/supreme-court-launches-digital-case-management-system/>) it supports the whole life of an appeal. In the last twelve months, [practice directions in force from 1 July 2026](<https://tribuneonlineng.com/supreme-court-launches-digital-case-management-system/>) have required counsel to upload processes and records of appeal to it. They start with appeals heard from September 2026. [The Federal High Court made filing electronic-only in its Lagos Division from 27 April 2026](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202604280230.html>). No source found since November 2023 says judgments or case status are open to the public online. Mature would need court decisions published online, or public look-up of case status online.

[The New Times reported](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/22773/news/law/justice-whats-new-in-upgraded-integrated-case-management-system>) that an upgraded Integrated Electronic Case Management System came into use in Rwanda from January 2025. [Lawyers trained in January 2025 file civil and criminal cases on the system](<https://www.certafoundation.rw/resource/enhancing-legal-practice-through-iecms-cja-staff-and-pro-bono-lawyers-training>). In the last twelve months, [the 13th Rwanda Governance Scorecard of October 2026](<https://rwandadispatch.com/rwandans-report-lower-satisfaction-with-public-services-new-scorecard-shows/>) rated electronic court filing services at 65.4% satisfaction, down 13.6 points on the previous assessment. No source found since November 2023 says judgments or case status are open to the public online. Mature would need court decisions published online or the public able to look up a case's status online.

[In July 2024 a former prosecutor told Atar](<https://atarnetwork.com/?p=2097>) that Sudan's judiciary had not adopted electronic archiving and still kept paper registers and forms. A former judge said the courts held no scans of case files, only litigants' names and case numbers and types. Fighting had destroyed court buildings and files in Khartoum and Omdurman. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A court computerisation project began in 2016, and nothing since says a system was rebuilt after the war. Preparing would need a case management or e-justice system procured, piloted in some courts or being built.

[Ecofin reported in August 2025](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2508-58308-senegal-advances-e-justice-rollout-with-dakar-area-pilot>) that the programme's final report records Senegal's e-Justice platform at the Pikine-Guédiawaye court, with five procedures digitised. In the last twelve months, [the justice ministry launched it officially on 10 September 2026](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Justice/modernisation-de-la-justice-les-plateformes-e-justice-et-jokko-ak-yoon-officiellement-lancees_n_503904.html>), to carry penal, civil, commercial and social cases. [In November 2026 the ministry gave courts 633 computers, scanners and printers for it](<https://fr.apanews.net/technologies/senegal-633-equipements-pour-la-justice-numerique/>). No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to be able to file cases or documents with the courts online.

No stage is set. The Justice App's case figures for Sierra Leone are dated 2022, and the app's 2017 pilot is older. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since November 2023 says how courts manage their cases. Preparing would need a source showing a case management or e-justice system procured, piloted in some courts or being built.

[Goobjoog reported](<https://en.goobjoog.com/somalia-launches-digital-case-management-system-to-modernize-justice-sector/>) the launch on 9 October 2025 of Somalia's Justice Sector Integrated Electronic Case Management System in Mogadishu. It links the CID, the prosecutor's office, the courts and the prison service in one electronic workflow. Officials say it replaces the paper process. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to be able to file cases or documents with the courts online.

[The Justice Policy director said in February 2024](<https://rstp.st/2024/02/22/governo-aposta-na-digitalizacao-da-justica-e-revisao-de-leis-para-reduzir-morosidade-de-crimes-sexuais/>) that the justice ministry of São Tomé and Príncipe is working with the company Sinergy on a reform aimed at electronic case processing in the courts. No date is given for it to go live. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[Eswatini's Integrated Electronic Case Management System was launched on 18 August 2025](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/new-digital-court-system-to-end-case-delays-prince-simelane/>) with training for users across the justice sector. It links the Judiciary, the ministry, the Law Society, police, the Anti-Corruption Commission and prisons. In the last twelve months, [on 22 May 2026 the project team showed the system's criminal, land and civil workflows to MPs](<https://swazi24.com/46158/news/digital-eswatini-team-presents-e-justice-system-to-mps/>). No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The Seychelles Judiciary launched phase one of an e-Service Platform in November 2025](<https://www.judiciary.sc/news/judiciary-launches-new-e-service-platform-to-streamline-access-to-justice/>), the first of a phased digital rollout. [Legal practitioners file written submissions online](<https://www.judiciary.sc/news/judiciary-launches-new-e-service-platform-to-streamline-access-to-justice/>) through it, with card payment and digital receipts. [Rules of September 2025](<https://www.nationalassembly.sc/sites/default/files/2025-11/SI%2072%202025%20-%20Electronic%20Filing%20of%20Written%20Submissions%20%28Civil%20Matters%29%20Regulations%202025_0.pdf>) allow electronic filing of written submissions in Supreme Court civil cases. No change has been found in the last twelve months beyond that launch. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The Ministry of Justice and UNDP launched a digital exchange platform in October 2025](<https://tribuneechos.com/e-justice-tchad-le-ministere-de-la-justice-lance-une-plateforme-dechange-numerique/>), with N'Djamena as the pilot court. It links litigants, lawyers and the judicial system in Chad. [A UNDP report says it sought a firm to build the platform in June 2024](<https://undpngddlsprod01.blob.core.windows.net/pdc/00105936-PPMR%C3%A9alisations_rapport.PDF>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

[The president of the Lomé commercial court said in February 2025](<https://tribunaldecommercedelome.tg/actualites/le-tribunal-de-commerce-de-lome-innove-avec-syscom>) that the court has handled commercial procedures on SYSCOM for six years. Lawyers, bailiffs and some individuals have filed online through it since December 2019. It also sends electronic notice of decisions. In the last twelve months, [the Lomé high court's portal, launched on 2 July 2026](<https://justice.gouv.tg/les-services-du-tribunal-de-grande-instance-de-lome-passent-en-mode-paiement-numerique/>), began letting litigants, lawyers and bailiffs follow procedures remotely.

[In November 2026 the Administrative Tribunal's central chambers held their first hearings on its Selim e-justice system](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/11/04/justice-le-tribunal-administratif-passe-a-laudience-electronique-avec-le-systeme-selim/>), La Presse reported. Its regional chambers were already digitised. [An African Development Bank notice of September 2025](<https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/aoi-tunisie-mise-en-place-dun-portail-de-services-e-justice-et-dune-application-metier-du-ministere-de-la-justice-tunisie-digitale-2020>) sought an e-Justice portal and business application for the Ministry of Justice. In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 a judicial council leader said digitising the Administrative Court's services had begun in part](<https://news-tunisia.tunisienumerique.com/justice-budget-digitalisation-court-delays-and-enforcement-of-rulings-at-the-centre-of-debate/>). No source found since November 2023 says lawyers or litigants can file with the courts online. Operating would need lawyers or litigants to file cases or documents online.

[In May 2025 the Judiciary's ICT Centre director said](<https://dailynews.co.tz/parliamentary-budget-committee-applauds-judiciarys-ict-reforms/>) cases are tracked on Tanzania's electronic system from the Court of Appeal to district courts. [Government Notice 609 of 2025](<https://media.tanzlii.org/media/legislation/381772/source_file/2ac18ebcc8a13636/tz-act-gn-2025-609-publication-document.pdf>), signed in October 2025, deems an electronically filed document filed once its court fee is paid. In the last twelve months, [the Chief Court Administrator said in February 2026](<https://dailynews.co.tz/courts-adopt-ai-integrated-data-systems/>) that litigants can file cases online from anywhere. He said they can also track a case's progress online. [In March 2026 the Chief Registrar said the system runs from District Courts to the Court of Appeal](<https://dailynews.co.tz/judiciary-reforms-boost-case-disposal-to-128pc/>).

Uganda's courts run ECCMIS, live since 1 March 2022, and [it was in 31 court stations by July 2025](<https://judiciary.go.ug/files/publications/doc_1783075331_341.pdf>). [The Judiciary says cases are filed and fees paid online](<https://judiciary.go.ug/files/publications/doc_1783075331_341.pdf>), and [a litigant at Jinja High Court checks her case file on her phone](<https://judiciary.go.ug/files/publications/doc_1783075331_341.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [it reached the Mbarara High Court circuit on 18 May 2026](<https://kalisho.info/mbarara-high-court-ushers-in-digital-transformation-as-eccmis-goes-live/>). [A Chief Justice circular of February 2026 made all filings in its courts electronic from 1 June](<https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/uganda-courts-to-go-paperless-starting-june-what-does-it-mean--5368378>). In October 2026 [its project manager said it is in more than 56 courts](<https://nilepost.co.ug/news/381759/judiciary-to-expand-digital-court-services-to-eight-courts-in-november>).

[The Minister of Justice said in September 2025](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/32920/>) that 19 South African High Courts had adopted Court Online, and that the first two went live in September 2022. [It went live in Gqeberha in July 2025](<https://justice.gov.za/m_speeches/2025/20250716-CourtOnline-DMin.html>), described as end-to-end case management. In the last twelve months, [a 2026 KwaZulu-Natal directive](<https://www.judiciary.org.za/images/Directives/Directives_2026/KZN%20Court%20Online%20Directives%20(Final%20June%202026).pdf>) has required practitioners and litigants there to upload process for issue on Court Online. No source found since November 2023 says judgments or case status are open to the public online. Mature would need court decisions published online or the public able to look up a case's status online.

[The Judiciary's contractor said in January 2025](<https://www.synisys.com/news/zambia-electronic-case-management-system/>) that Zambia's electronic case management system is to link the Supreme, Constitutional, Appeal, High and Subordinate Courts. Treasury funds it, and the courts still worked by hand. In the last twelve months, [on 31 October 2026 the Judiciary launched the system nationwide](<https://times.co.zm/judiciary-rolls-out-nationwide-electronic-case-management-system/>), starting with a pilot in four registries in Lusaka and Kitwe. [The Chief Justice opened training for it on 2 November](<https://diamondtvzambia.com/chief-justice-opens-training-ahead-of-digital-court-system-rollout/>). No source found since November 2023 says a court case management system is in service in any court. Establishing would need a case management system in service in some courts or one tier.

Zimbabwe's courts run the Integrated Electronic Case Management System, begun in 2022, which [now serves the Constitutional, Supreme, Labour and High Courts](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/electronic-case-management-system-iecms-brings-justice-closer-to-gweru-residents/>). [Litigants and legal practitioners file documents electronically](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/electronic-case-management-system-iecms-brings-justice-closer-to-gweru-residents/>), and court users can track their cases, the minister said in September 2026. In the last twelve months, [rural courts in Chipinge and Chimanimani joined in January 2026](<https://postonsunday.co.zw/2026/01/22/a-new-electronic-court-system-can-bridge-the-divide-for-people-in-the-countryside/>). [In June 2026 it reached 16 more magistrates' courts in Mashonaland East and Manicaland](<https://www.masvingomirror.com/justice-gwaunza-launches-phase-4-3-iecms/>). From October 2026 it is reaching Magistrates' Courts, with Harare and Bulawayo planned by year-end.
